title: AI Risk Management Framework FAQs | NIST

policy_extraction.issuing_body: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)
covered_actors: Developers, users, and evaluators of AI systems (AI actors)
Public and private sector organizations of all sizes in any sector

evidence.quote: The Framework is intended to help developers, users and evaluators of AI systems better manage AI risks which could affect individuals, organizations, society, or the environment.

The Framework users and AI actors should consider and encompass trustworthiness characteristics during pre-design, design and development, deployment, use, and test and evaluation of AI technologies and systems.

Will private or public sector organizations be required to use the Framework?
No. NIST has produced the AI RMF as a voluntary Framework.

evidence.quote: Organizations seeking specific guidance for how to achieve AI RMF function outcomes may borrow as many – or as few – suggestions as apply to their industry use case or interests.
evidence.source_section: Will NIST provide additional guidance to help with using the AI RMF?

policy_extraction.implementation_notes: Official NIST AI RMF FAQ companion page (initial publication 2021-07-13, updated through the January 26, 2023 AI RMF 1.0 release). Clarifies the Framework's voluntary non-binding status, broad scalability across public and private sectors, seven trustworthiness characteristics and their tradeoffs, development timeline (2021 RFI through Jan 2023 launch), and relationship to the companion Playbook and other NIST frameworks.

risk_framing.rationale_summary: The AI RMF FAQs are dominantly framed around innovation_enablement, presenting a voluntary, scalable, non-mandatory standards framework aimed at fostering innovative approaches to trustworthiness, improving measurement science, and building confidence in AI systems. Innovation_enablement leads consumer_public_safety, which is a strong runner-up focused on managing AI risks to individuals, organizations, society, and quality of life through safe, valid, and reliable systems. Economic_competitiveness ('enhance economic security') and fundamental_rights ('privacy-enhanced, and fair with harmful bias managed') serve as clear secondary frames, with a minor national_security nod to NSCAI recommendations.
